Credits, Usage & Spend Limits ​

A credit is one US dollar. The wallet is a USD balance that every settled LLM call decrements by what that call cost, and the ledger beside it is the append-only record of why. Everything on this page sits on top of metering that already exists: the run's usageLog records what a call spent whether or not a wallet is watching.

Credits are a hosted-platform concern. In local / bring-your-own-key mode the wallet is never consulted — you pay the provider directly — so the gates below that read the wallet are no-ops. In cloud mode the platform pays for the tokens, so an empty wallet always stops work.

How usage is metered ​

Every settled LLM call produces a token record:

FieldMeaning
inputTokensFresh input tokens
cacheReadTokensInput served from cache
cacheCreationTokensInput written to cache (billed at its own rate)
outputTokensGenerated tokens
costUsdThe settled price, when the provider reported one
unreportedThe call ran but no request reported a token — zeros here are an absent measurement, not a measurement of zero

The engine folds that record into the run twice: as one RunUsageEntry appended to run.usageLog, and as a running total on the participant that made the call. A call that moved tokens but carries no costUsd is stamped unpriced and counted on the participant's unpricedCalls, so a total can always say how much of itself was never costed. An unpriced call is never rendered as free.

Separately, each thread message carries its own settled vitals (RunEventStats) — tokens, wall-clock ms, context occupancy, model, and cost. Because providers bill a turn once rather than per message, a multi-message turn's cost is apportioned across its messages and flagged costShared, so the UI can say "share of a turn" instead of presenting an estimate as an invoice.

Three call classes are metered, all through the same accounting:

  • Run delegations and PRIME's run turns — into the run's usageLog, then the wallet.
  • Main-chat turns (dashboard chat, Telegram and other channels) — straight to the wallet with ledger reason chat.usage.
  • Side calls (the memory curator, and any other post-turn helper) — routed by ambient scope: inside a run they land in that run's ledger, outside one they hit the wallet. These are small per call but fire constantly, which is exactly the shape of spend that otherwise goes unnoticed.

The wallet and the ledger ​

memory/credits.json        ← wallet snapshot (local dev fallback only)
memory/credit-ledger.jsonl ← one JSON object per line, append-safe

MongoDB is the authoritative store: CreditWalletModel (keyed default locally, by orgId in cloud) and CreditLedgerModel. The files above are written only when Mongo is unreachable in local development; in cloud mode a persist attempt with no DB is refused and logged rather than silently accepted.

The wallet update is an atomic aggregation-pipeline $add floored with $max at zero, upserted, with the returned document treated as authoritative. That matters with more than one instance running: a concurrent debit from another process cannot be lost to a last-writer-wins overwrite of a process-local balance.

The balance can never go below zero — not by debit, not by adjustment, not by a call that costs more than what is left. A persisted legacy negative balance is normalised to zero on load.

Each ledger entry is immutable:

FieldMeaning
idBase-36 millisecond prefix + UUID (roughly sortable, collision-resistant)
atTimestamp
deltaWhat actually moved in the wallet — negative for a debit, positive for a top-up
reasonrun.usage · chat.usage · topup.manual · adjustment · grant.admin · revoke.admin
runIdThe run the debit belongs to (run.usage only)
actorWhich participant's call it was — pairs with the run's log
orgId / userIdOwning workspace and acting member (cloud)
rawCostUsdThe provider's raw cost before margin
modelsEvery model the settled call reported
balanceAfterThe balance once the entry was applied

delta and rawCostUsd deliberately differ when a final debit is truncated by the zero floor: delta describes the wallet movement, rawCostUsd still records the full provider cost. Between runId and actor, every line traces back to a run and from there to the exact calls that produced it.

The in-memory ledger keeps the most recent 500 entries; the API clamps a requested limit to that. The files and the database keep everything.

Margin ​

creditsMargin (a system setting, default 1, minimum 1) multiplies costUsd on debit. 1 means the wallet is charged at cost; a value above 1 is a managed margin. The charged amount is rounded to six decimal places — well below the price of a single token — to stop float drift accumulating on a running balance.

charged = round6(costUsd × max(creditsMargin, 1))

The same margin is applied to the run cost that per-run ceilings compare against, so the ceiling and the ledger agree on what a run has spent.

The caps that exist ​

CapWhere it livesDefaultEffect when crossed
Wallet balanceThe workspace wallet—Refuses new work (cloud only)
monthlyCreditBudgetMember limits0 (unlimited)Refuses new work; pauses a live run
extraCreditGrantMember limits0One-time top-up on this month's budget
perRunCostCapUsdMember limits0 (off)Pauses the run
maxConcurrentRunsMember limits, then org limits0 (member) / 3 (org)Refuses a new run
maxEffortMember limits'' (none)Clamps the request down — never rejects
turnMaxCostUsdSystem settings5Pauses the run after one over-budget call
runCostAlertUsdSystem settings0 (off)Local mode: a global per-run ceiling that pauses the run

Two things to note. Effort is the only dial that degrades rather than stopping: a member capped at medium who asks for high silently gets medium. And turnMaxCostUsd is enforced against the price Saidi settled on, which is why it still holds on a custom endpoint where the SDK's own budget parameter would be denominated in a rate table the ledger does not use.

Where the gates fire ​

Before a run starts. In order: the workspace must be active and not suspended; the wallet must be non-empty; the member's monthly budget must have room; the member and the org must be under their concurrency caps. Any failure throws a human-readable error the caller surfaces — a route, a PRIME tool, a cron, a reflex, a Telegram message. On success the run start is counted on the member's monthly counter.

Before every billable call. A lighter check runs on the hot paths — main chat, existing runs, channels, nested agent calls. It looks at spend eligibility only: the wallet, and the acting member's monthly budget. Membership caching is ~30 seconds so this does not add a database query per tool call.

This check fails closed. A missing membership means the person was removed and may not keep spending. A transient database error blocks spend with Usage checks are temporarily unavailable — please retry in a moment. rather than letting an unhandled rejection escape a fire-and-forget path. System automations and platform superadmins bypass it.

After every settled call. The debit lands, then the wallet is re-checked, then the member's per-run and monthly caps are evaluated asynchronously. A crossed cap pauses the run.

What a blocked run actually does ​

The pause path is deliberately the same shape as every other budget stop: a SYSTEM event is appended to the run thread with the reason, and the run is moved to paused — never cancelled. Pausing preserves the resumable-run semantics described in Runs: the plan, the branch, the sessions and the in-flight record all survive, and resuming picks up where it stopped.

The model is told too, and told plainly. Every delegation tool — PRIME's delegate and delegate_batch, a lead's delegate_to_specialist / delegate_to_specialists, delegate_to_project, and the ask path — checks the gate before dispatching and, when it is blocked, returns the block text as an error tool result. The model does not get a generic "something failed"; it gets one of:

Insufficient credits: the wallet balance is $0.00. Ask your workspace owner to
add credits to continue.
Your monthly usage budget ($25.00) is used up — it resets next month, or an
admin can raise it.
You are no longer a member of this workspace.

Mid-run pauses, which happen after a debit rather than before a dispatch, produce their own wording:

Run paused: its cost reached your per-run cap of $10.00. An admin can raise the
cap, then resume the run.
Run paused: your monthly usage budget ($25.00) is used up — it resets next
month, or an admin can raise it.
Run paused: its owner is no longer a member of this workspace — an admin can
remove or reassign it.

And the per-call ceiling, which names the setting so the fix is obvious:

<actor> settled at $6.2100 for one call, over the $5 per-turn ceiling. Paused —
raise CALL COST CEILING in Settings → Costs & Limits, or resume to continue.

In local mode there is no membership and therefore no per-member cap, but a runaway run can still burn tokens. runCostAlertUsd doubles as a real global per-run pause ceiling there. It is opt-in — 0 means off, and local behaviour is unchanged until you set it:

Run paused: its cost reached the per-run ceiling of $12.00 (runCostAlertUsd).
Raise the ceiling in Settings, then resume the run.

Metering itself never breaks work. Debiting, member counters and the mid-run cap evaluation are all best-effort and swallow their own errors — bookkeeping must not be the reason a run fails.

Reading a balance ​

GET /api/credits returns what the asking member can still spend, which is not necessarily the wallet balance. A configured monthly budget is a hard ceiling even when the shared wallet holds more:

available = min(walletBalance, (monthlyCreditBudget + extraCreditGrant) − spentThisMonth)

With no monthly budget configured, the wallet is the only ceiling and the response reports limited: false.

GET /api/credits/usage?limit=N returns the wallet plus the detailed ledger, and requires the billing.view or usage.viewOrg permission. Both endpoints are cloud only. After every debit or top-up a wallet observer notifies dashboards with an amount-free invalidation, and each client re-fetches its own scoped balance.

Topping up and raising a cap ​

Adding credits is a superadmin action on the platform plane:

http
POST /api/admin/orgs/:id/credits
Content-Type: application/json

{ "amount": 250 }

A positive amount is a grant (ledger reason grant.admin), a negative amount a revocation (revoke.admin). The amount must be non-zero and no larger than 100,000 in magnitude, and the acting superadmin's user id is recorded on the entry. The response returns the new balance. This is the manual-billing path; the store's older topUp method is retained only for migrations and store-level tests.

Raising a member's cap means editing that member's limits — monthlyCreditBudget, extraCreditGrant, perRunCostCapUsd, maxEffort, maxConcurrentRuns. extraCreditGrant is the right dial for "give this person more room this month" without permanently moving their budget. Governance records are cached for about 30 seconds and the cache is invalidated on an admin edit, so a change applies promptly rather than at the next cache expiry.

Operator-wide dials — creditsMargin, turnMaxCostUsd, runCostAlertUsd — live in system settings; see Configuration.

After raising whatever stopped it, resume the paused run. Nothing needs re-planning: the run was paused, not cancelled.
